definition: Meticulous means extremely careful about small details.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word meticulous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know meticulous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The wedding planner was meticulous about the seating plan, spacing the feuding cousins to the exact table.
A careful cook checks the big things; a meticulous one logs the water temperature to the half degree.
Fanatical goes past meticulous — care swollen into creed, continued long after the details have stopped repaying it.

Precise means exact where exactness can be measured — the right number, the right word, a tolerance met. Meticulous is wider: extreme care spent on every small detail, measurable or not. A precise figure can come carelessly off a good instrument; meticulous work shows the care itself.

Thorough means complete in coverage — every item visited once, nothing on the list skipped. Meticulous cares about depth instead: it lingers over the fine grain of each thing. A sweep can be thorough without pausing anywhere; meticulous work slows down exactly where the details grow small.
lets details slip unexamined
rushed work, with the details left to fend for themselves
Latin metus, "fear," built no other common English word — meticulous carries the root alone. Even its own original timid sense faded, leaving only the careful one.
Meticulous means extremely careful about small details.

The film was set in 1943, and the meticulous prop master furnished the detective's desk as if the camera might read it: a phone book printed for the right city and year, the half-smoked cigarette brand the script named, pencils sharpened to wartime length, a blotter aged with tea.
None of it holds the shot for more than a second.
Meticulous is the exact word because the prop master is extremely careful about small details — care spent down at the grain of the work, where most eyes never go.
This unit's fastidious describes the judge whom nothing satisfies; meticulous describes the maker who satisfies even that judge.
The care is spent on the work itself, one small correct thing at a time.
Meticulous is praise for care at the grain — the maker's virtue.

Keep the family straight: this unit's fastidious describes the impossible-to-please judge, methodical the ordered steps, and scrupulous adds a conscience — a meticulous forger is entirely possible; a scrupulous one is a contradiction.
When the wonder is how small the attended details are, meticulous.

Film crews joke that nobody sees the props department's best work, and Marisol Vega proves the joke true.
For the liner scene she reproduced a 1912 dinner menu: the flourish under the soup course, the slightly uneven letterpress bite, the gilt edge worn just where a thumb would hold it.
She is meticulous on principle.
The camera would pass the menu in half a second, but she matched the paper stock by weight and aged the ink for a week.
A producer once asked why she bothered.
Vega answered that an audience can't name what's right in a frame, only feel it.
When the film opened, a maritime historian wrote to ask where the studio had found an original menu.
